# .github/ — CI standard and release lane

- **The gate.** The `main-protection` ruleset gates the merge and its live required-check list is the single authority — read it with `gh api repos/developerz-ai/wurk/rulesets`; never re-declare the list here or in any doc. The gated jobs gate per-step, never per-job, so they always run and report — GitHub counts a skipped required job as passing.
- **Cheap by construction.** **One** full Ruby suite run per PR is the required check, on the newest Ruby + newest Rails, with the coverage gate folded in (`COVERAGE=1` on the same invocation). A docs-only PR (`*.md`, `docs/**`, `.dz/**`) runs `test/guards.txt` in that required job instead; it still reports. A `guards` job answers first on a code change, and the compat legs wait on it.
- **The `compat` matrix** in `test.yml` is not required: gemspec Ruby floor (`3.2`) × newest Rails, newest Ruby × oldest supported Rails (`7.1`), newest Ruby × newest Rails on Valkey, and on Dragonfly v1.34.0 with stock Lua settings. Each runs the full suite without `COVERAGE=1`, on PRs touching Ruby and on the daily schedule. Rubocop's `TargetRubyVersion: 3.2` holds the floor for syntax only; this matrix is what holds it at runtime.
- **Runners.** Jobs run on GitHub-hosted runners (free for a public repo) — `ubuntu-latest` for every job except `test.yml`'s `python-client`, pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` because actions/python-versions publishes no Python 3.9 build for Ubuntu 26.04, which `ubuntu-latest` now resolves to; the image is what moves, never the matrix (`python-client (3.9)` is the required check name). There are no self-hosted runners and no runner variables, so a fork PR never reaches persistent hardware, and outside contributors' runs still wait on the repo's approval policy (`all_external_contributors`).
- **Duplicate pushes.** In `test.yml`, `ecosystem.yml` and `topology.yml`, `detect` runs `bin/ci-dup-push`: a push to `main` whose tree byte-equals a PR head that already passed that workflow skips the gated jobs, and any doubt falls open to a full run.
- **Concurrency and timeouts.** Every workflow declares a `concurrency` group and every job that runs steps sets `timeout-minutes`; PR runs cancel in progress, and deploy/publish workflows never auto-cancel. `main` runs never cancel in `test.yml` and `topology.yml`, where each commit has its own group; `ecosystem.yml` keeps one group, for its release watcher, so a queued `main` run there can be replaced.
- **Workflow lint.** The `actionlint` job (pinned by SHA, gated per-step on a `workflows` paths-filter) and `spec-docs` always report, and `zizmor` audits workflows. A schedule-only `canary` job runs Ruby head (non-failing) and 3.4. Install actionlint locally when editing workflows: `cd ~/.local/bin && bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhysd/actionlint/main/scripts/download-actionlint.bash)`; zizmor is `uv tool install zizmor`.
- **Reusable workflows hold only what the caller grants.** A caller job that omits a permission the callee asks for ends `startup_failure` with nothing executed, and nothing reports it until the next release (#617 broke the release lane; #858 found it; #859 fixed it).
- **Bench.** The bot comments deltas on PRs that touch Ruby or bench inputs (`bench.yml`'s path filter). A regression past the noise-adjusted 5% threshold (both runs' error bounds plus 5%) is flagged in the comment and fails the `bench vs base` job, which is not a required check and so never blocks a merge: hosted-runner noise would make a hard gate flaky. `bin/bench-compare` owns the rule. `bench.yml`'s `commands per job` job is the exception: deterministic, so it hard-fails on any added per-job Redis command (baseline in `bench/command_count.rb`, published in `docs/benchmarks.md`); it is not a required check either.
- **The release tag is an output, never an input.** `release.yml` fires on a `lib/wurk/version.rb` bump landing on `main` — *not* on a tag push — derives the tag from `Wurk::VERSION` (`ReleaseHelpers.git_tag_for`), publishes the gem, and only then cuts the tag + GitHub Release, which then calls `deploy-demo` and the release smoke. `build` runs third-party code with no credential, `publish` alone holds `id-token: write`, `release` alone holds `contents: write`, and preflight's `publish`/`finish` outputs let a re-run finish a partly done release. Never re-add a `tags:` trigger: a tag as input let anything that could push one (the `developerz-ai[bot]` maintainer agent did, seven times) turn the release lane red and leave a gem-less GitHub Release marked "Latest". Full rationale in `RELEASE.md`.
- **Deploys.** `deploy-demo.yml` builds and pushes the demo image on `main` pushes touching what it runs; an image updater rolls it, CI holds no cluster credentials, and the run fails if `/demo/build` does not report the built commit. `pages.yml` publishes the site, `publish-wiki.yml` the wiki. A merge deploys nothing else, and the gem ships only on a version bump. `audit.yml` is a weekly advisory dependency check.

`attest.yml` attaches and attests an SBOM after `release` completes. It is separate because RubyGems trusts `release.yml` with no environment, so an `id-token` there could publish; keep OIDC out of `release.yml` apart from `publish`.
